status: Proposed commercial architecture. No approved numeric price list, billing activation or measured unit economics.
decision: Free fictional demo; paid annual Core, Expand and Enterprise subscriptions; separately priced onboarding and custom work.
rationale: A fixed two-week customer-data trial can consume delivery work before enough evidence exists to judge value.
A free fictional demo supports evaluation without committing RADR to unpaid data integration or ongoing processing.
A platform minimum protects the fixed cost of serving an account. Named locations allow expansion without seat friction.
An explicit usage allowance protects against unbounded processing, refresh and support costs.
Onboarding and custom work need their own scope and economics rather than an implied unlimited inclusion.
Keep evidence and human review common to every scope. Package by operational coverage, not by withholding trust.
Do not charge a percentage of modeled savings. Subscription fees and customer-value estimates are different quantities.

recurringQuote.structure: Annual platform minimum + contracted location coverage + scoped processing/support requirements
recurringQuote.restaurantBasis: Named operating locations, selected priorities, source complexity and usage
recurringQuote.hotelBasis: Named properties, room/data scale, selected priorities, source complexity and usage
includedAllowanceMustDefine: Processing and media workloads where applicable
recurringQuote.term: Annual; billing schedule, renewal and cancellation agreed in writing
recurringQuote.growth: New sites, higher usage or additional work require approved scope and price changes. No automatic overage billing is implemented.

rules: State included hours/deliverables, dependencies and acceptance criteria
Do not discount setup below its cost without recording an explicit acquisition investment

costFloor.recurring: minimum monthly-equivalent subscription = monthly direct delivery cost / (1 - target recurring gross margin)
costFloor.setup: minimum setup fee = direct setup delivery cost / (1 - target setup gross margin)
costFloor.cacPaybackMonths: (acquisition cost + unrecovered setup cost) / monthly recurring gross profit
costFloor.grossProfit: Subscription revenue less direct recurring delivery costs. This excludes R&D, general overhead and taxes and is not net profit.
costFloor.constraint: The price must also pass willingness-to-pay and evidenced customer-value validation; a cost floor alone does not prove demand or profitability.

sensitivityExamples.label: Illustrative arithmetic in arbitrary currency units. These are invented cost scenarios, not RADR costs, quotes or customer results.

validationBeforeNumericPricing: Measure direct delivery costs for representative restaurant and hotel scopes, including heavy usage.
Estimate setup labor and custom-source maintenance without hiding them in gross margin.
Test quote acceptance and objections with qualified prospects, then track activation, support load and renewal intent.
Compare realized contribution and acquisition payback by scope; revise the minimum or included allowance when costs change.
Do not describe these assumptions as maximized profit, validated willingness to pay or a guaranteed return.

marketEvidence.observation: Quotes depend on module selection and customer requirements.
Per-room basis and tailored quotes; some add-ons and payment processing are separate.
Starter, Growth and Premium packages with quote CTAs and separately described add-ons.
Public tier ladder with defined invoice/integration allowances and priced add-ons.
Custom quote based on the selected restaurant software scope.

evidenceLimits: Public pricing pages only; no access to competitor contracts, discounts, margins or internal costs. No claim that all providers prohibit trials.
quoteReviewRules: Prefer annual prepayment for cash flow; state any agreed installment schedule explicitly.
Do not offer a blanket annual or volume discount before checking the resulting gross margin and acquisition payback.
Only reduce the location rate where scale reduces delivery cost or the approved commercial case supports the reduction.
Cost a high-usage case as well as the typical case; do not promise unlimited processing, media ingestion or support.
Treat any waived onboarding as acquisition investment with a named budget, not as zero delivery cost.
Review customer acceptance and retention alongside margin; a higher headline price or longer contract does not by itself maximize profit.
